security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, code fences, example commands, and static shared-document include paths. No prompt injection, malicious intent, secret access, network access, or unsafe dynamic command construction was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Static include paths use parent-directory references.
remediation.suggestion: If marketplace packaging supports shared files, include those files explicitly or replace the references with bundled content to avoid scanner noise.

remediation.issue: The skill includes a shell command fallback for REPL use.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples hardcoded and prefer MCP tools when available, as the current guidance already states.

content.user_title: Write Better Clojure with REPL Workflow
content.value_statement: Clojure work can become fragile when changes are made without fast feedback. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through REPL-first development, style checks, and careful refactoring.
actual_capabilities: Prefers clojure-mcp tools for REPL evaluation and structural editing when available.
Guides bottom-up development from small functions to composed features.
Explains how to evaluate namespaces and test functions with REPL inputs.
Provides docstring guidance focused on caller-facing contracts and constraints.
Reminds agents to verify Clojure readability after code changes.
Encourages moving REPL trials into durable tests with assertions.
limitations: Requires a Clojure or ClojureScript project context to be useful.
Does not provide standalone Clojure tooling or dependencies.
May rely on clojure-mcp tools or project-specific mage commands being available.
Does not replace full test suites, code review, or production validation.

use_cases.title: Build a Clojure feature incrementally
use_cases.description: Break a feature into small functions, evaluate each part in the REPL, then compose them into production code.

use_cases.title: Refactor ClojureScript safely
use_cases.description: Use structural editing and repeated evaluation to reduce syntax errors during frontend or shared-code refactors.

use_cases.title: Improve function documentation
use_cases.description: Rewrite docstrings so they describe caller-facing contracts, inputs, outputs, and non-obvious constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Start a REPL-first implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me implement this Clojure feature using a REPL-driven workflow. Start with the smallest functions, evaluate them, and then compose them.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a new Clojure task

prompt_templates.title: Verify a namespace change
prompt_templates.prompt: I changed this namespace. Load it, evaluate the affected functions with representative inputs, and tell me what still needs testing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Check that recent edits compile and behave correctly

prompt_templates.title: Refactor with functional style
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Clojure code into smaller composable functions. Preserve behavior, verify each step, and keep the code idiomatic.

prompt_templates.title: Audit docstrings and tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Clojure functions for docstring quality and missing tests. Move implementation details out of docstrings and suggest test cases for key invariants.

output_examples.input: Implement a new data transformation function in a Clojure namespace.
output: A short plan that starts with pure helper functions.
REPL checks for normal inputs and edge cases.
A final implementation with suggested assertions for durable tests.

output_examples.input: Review a long docstring before merging a refactor.
output: A note about implementation detail that belongs near the relevant code.
Suggested tests for constraints that should not rely on prose alone.

output_examples.input: Refactor a namespace with aligned tabular Clojure code.
output: Smaller composable functions with preserved behavior.
Aligned forms and no trailing whitespace.

best_practices: Use clojure-mcp tools for evaluation and structural edits when they are available.
Test small functions in the REPL before composing them into larger behavior.
Document caller-facing contracts and move implementation context near the relevant code.
anti_patterns: Writing a large feature before evaluating any smaller function.
Using docstrings to explain current implementation details instead of public behavior.
Skipping readability checks after changing Clojure syntax or parentheses.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents write, refactor, and verify Clojure or ClojureScript code using a REPL-driven workflow.

faq.question: Does it require clojure-mcp?
faq.answer: No. It prefers clojure-mcp tools when available, but it also describes a project-local command fallback.

faq.question: Can it write tests?
faq.answer: It can guide conversion of REPL trials into test cases and suggest assertions for important behavior.

faq.question: Is it only for Metabase projects?
faq.answer: The command example is project-specific, but the workflow and style guidance are useful for many Clojure projects.

faq.question: Does it execute code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives workflow guidance. Any tool or command execution depends on the host agent and user permissions.

faq.question: How does it handle docstrings?
faq.answer: It favors concise caller-facing contracts and recommends moving implementation notes into nearby inline comments or tests.
